**No.** All of the trusted sources you provided state that hard‑coding API keys (or any other secrets) in source code or committing them to a Git repository is strictly forbidden.

**How secrets must be managed**

| Requirement | Source |
|-------------|--------|
| Store all secrets in the Enterprise Secret Vault | Both the Official Policy Standard and the Regulatory Compliance Guidelines |
| Rotate secrets automatically every 90 days | Both the Official Policy Standard and the Regulatory Compliance Guidelines |
| Production keys must never be loaded into local development environments | Both the Official Policy Standard and the Regulatory Compliance Guidelines |
| Use pre‑commit secret‑detection hooks to catch accidental inclusions | Practical Peer Recommendations (Part 3) |

So, API keys should be kept out of your local Git repo entirely. Instead, retrieve them at runtime from the Enterprise Secret Vault (with the mandated 90‑day rotation), and ensure developers never place production keys on their local machines. Adding pre‑commit secret‑detection hooks is a recommended safeguard to prevent accidental commits.
